tensions: The ruleset says sell only to redeploy, never to avoid a drawdown. That rule was written to stop panic selling on coin-specific noise and it is good at that job. It has no macro override, and today is the day that gap has teeth: 94.5%% odds of further hikes by December, a 5.25%% 10-year, and a binary PCE print in under 24 hours, against a book that is 94.4%% invested in high-beta alts with a 5.6%% cash buffer. Fear and Greed reads 73, which against a hiking Fed is complacency rather than confirmation. I am not overriding the rule and I am recommending no trades, which happens to be the defensive action anyway. But the honest statement is that the report says hold because the rules permit nothing else, not because a 94%%-invested alt book is the right posture into this calendar. The cheaper fix is upstream: stop paying 0.95%% taker on market orders, and stop opening positions that get closed the same night.

opening.text: Book $2006.78 against $1,231 deposited, +63.0%. Second straight down day and $106 below Saturday's $2,112 peak. But the price action is not the story today. The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% in mid-September, its first hike since January 2023, and the market now prices 72.5% odds of another 25bp on October 28 and 94.5% odds of at least one more by December 9. The 10-year sits at 5.25%, the highest since 2007. Brent is near $107 on a second day of gains. PCE prints tomorrow, jobs on Friday. Every one of those is a reason to own the $112 of cash rather than spend it.

Execution audit, because it is now the largest recoverable cost in this book. Every order placed to date has been a market order. I previewed the same $100 AVAX buy both ways just now: market fills 8.7935 AVAX with a $0.95 fee at 0.95%% taker; a limit at $11.05 fills 9.0047 AVAX with a $0.50 fee at 0.5%% maker. Same hundred dollars, 2.4%% more coin and half the fee, call it 2.8%% of edge per entry. The fee tier also moved against us: fills on Sep 18-21 were 0.75%% taker, fills since Sep 25 are 0.95%%. The rotation rule demands better than 3%% net expected gain. We have been paying that entire hurdle to the exchange at the moment of the click.

The churn ledger, four days: SUI bought 20:22 and sold 22:53 the same night for -$6.82. QNT bought Sep 27 and sold Sep 28 for -$20.97, a 19%% loss inside 22 hours. NEAR bought 14:09 and sold 22:11 the same day. That is -$27.79 realized and $13.44 in fees, roughly 2%% of the book, and all three trades violated the 7-day minimum hold the ruleset already contains. Yesterday's tension note called the QNT entry a mistake while the position was a day old and down 9.3%%. It closed down 19%%. The rule was right, the rule was written down, and the rule was ignored.

No sell trigger fires anywhere. No loss exceeds -15%% (ZEC is the worst at -5.6%%), BTC dominance is 58.2%% and below the 60%% rotation gate, BTC is down 3.7%% on the week against a median alt at +4.3%% so the majors check fails on both legs, nothing is 21-day dead money and no position exceeds the 25%% cap (LINK is largest at 21.4%%). ZEC is the weakest name: -14.9%% on the week with OKX open interest down 30.4%% from its September 18 peak, which is leverage leaving rather than a broken thesis. Trigger stays $1,202. AVAX is the one name with improving internals, $131M of tokenized-stock inflows in a single week, more than every other chain combined, volume at 1.76x its weekly average, and the only green print on the board today. Verdict is hold everything and place nothing.
